facts: Sam Bankman-Fried founded the FTX cryptocurrency exchange and the trading firm Alameda Research.
He was convicted of all seven criminal counts of fraud, conspiracy, and money laundering related to the collapse of FTX.
On March 28, 2024, Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison and ordered to forfeit $11 billion.
FTX, Alameda Research, and over 130 associated legal entities declared bankruptcy in November 2022 following a massive withdrawal of customer assets.
John J. Ray III replaced Bankman-Fried as CEO of FTX after the company filed for bankruptcy.
Bankman-Fried graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2014 with a bachelor's degree in physics and a minor in mathematics.
